items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We were joined by John Coleman, Jr., on C melody sax... It was the first time that Smittie and Edgar had been on an encampment... I had a wonderful time and it was the first time that most of us making the music had played for an audience

ctx.x: But getting back to the encampment, Smittie, Edgar and I arrived in Centerville and was taken to the farm where this get together was taking place and which happened to be on millionaire Hagen's farm, where I had stayed with Aunty Amanda Sparks some years before.

We were joined by John Coleman, Jr., on C melody sax and a drummer from Georgetown whose name was James Coleman, but he was not related to my clan. It was the first time that Smittie and Edgar had been on an encampment and I think it was the first time Edgar had really been in the country as he was born in Cincinnati. Smittie had some relatives in Lexington which was not far from the site of the camp and quite a few people would come from Lexington and Paris to dance and return home when the dancing stopped.

I had a wonderful time and it was the first time that most of us making the music had played for an audience of dancers and listeners except Smittie, and I remember the first ad lib phrase that I played without rehearsing, was a thing that had been sung by someone which said, 'somebody gone tore their breeches', and this is how it would be written and I felt really proud of myself.
